title: Functorial K-injective Hom and scalar telescopes agree on every leg
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the module universe [def-weil-size-convention], let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings, and assume filtered colimits of $R$-module sheaves are exact. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], integer-indexed cochain complexes and the localization $Q$ to their unbounded derived category $D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $s$ be a global section of $R$, and let $A,P$ be arbitrary complexes of $R$-module sheaves. Fix a functorial K-injective resolution $i_B:B\to I(B)$ as in [def-pur-derived-internal-hom, def-pur-kinjective-complex]; the functor $I$ is not assumed $R$-linear. Form the internal Hom complex [def-pur-hom-complex]
$$X=\mathcal Hom_R^\bullet(A,I(P)),$$
and its chain endomorphisms $t_1=\mathcal Hom_R^\bullet(A,I(s_P))$ and $t_2=s_X$, where $s_P,s_X$ denote multiplication by $s$. Then $t_1$ and $t_2$ are chain-homotopic. For $k=1,2$ let $C_k$ be the termwise colimit of $X\xrightarrow{t_k}X\xrightarrow{t_k}\cdots$, with colimit legs $j_n^{(k)}:X\to C_k$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. There exists an isomorphism
$$\gamma:Q(C_1)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(C_2)\quad\text{such that}\quad\gamma\circ Q(j_n^{(1)})=Q(j_n^{(2)})\quad(n\geq0).$$
Thus the tower obtained by applying the fixed functorial internal-Hom representative $\mathcal Hom_R^\bullet(A,I(-))$ to $(P,s_P)$ and the scalar tower on $X$ have isomorphic colimits in $D(R)$, with this compatibility for every leg, including the zeroth. Neither $A$, $P$, nor $X$ is required to be bounded, and no continuity hypothesis on derived internal Hom is imposed.

proof.text: Put $J=I(P)$, $a=I(s_P)$ and $b=s_J$. Naturality of the augmentation and $R$-linearity of its components give $a i_P=i_P s_P=b i_P$. Since $i_P$ is a quasi-isomorphism, cancellation of the invertible $Q(i_P)$ gives $Q(a)=Q(b)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] with source and target both $J$: the target is K-injective by the fixed resolution hypothesis, so injectivity of the map from homotopy classes to derived morphisms yields a degree $-1$ sheaf-module map $h:J\to J$ with $a-b=d_Jh+hd_J$. This uses naturality of $i$, with no scalar-linearity assumption on $I$.

source.place: Tag 070I (lemma-K-injective), (1) implies (3); naturality of the fixed resolution augmentation.

proof.text: For a degree $n$ local section $f=(f^p)_p$ of $X$, define $H(f)^p=h^{p+n}f^p$. This defines an $R$-linear degree $-1$ map of sheaves and commutes with restriction, component by component. Using the differential in [def-pur-hom-complex], $d_X(Hf)=d_Jhf+(-1)^n hf d_A$ and $H(d_Xf)=hd_Jf-(-1)^n hf d_A$. Adding gives $(d_XH+Hd_X)f=(d_Jh+hd_J)f=(a-b)f$. Postcomposition with $a$ is $t_1$, and postcomposition with $b=s_J$ is multiplication by $s$ on $X$, namely $t_2$. Thus $t_1-t_2=d_XH+Hd_X$. No interchange of a product with a colimit is used.

proof.text: Apply [lem-kun-complex-colimit-hocolim] to each sequential system $(X,t_k)$ of $R$-module sheaves. The indexing category $\mathbf N$ is small in the module universe and filtered, so the assumed exact filtered colimits apply to this sequence. Its termwise colimit is the specified $C_k$; neither boundedness nor monic transitions are required. Write $B=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}X$, with inclusions $e_n$, and $u_ke_n=e_n-e_{n+1}t_k$. In the cone convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], put $T_k=\operatorname{Cone}(u_k)$, with $T_k^r=B^r\oplus B^{r+1}$ and $d_k(b,c)=(d_Bb+u_kc,-d_Bc)$. The cited telescope lemma supplies the canonical quasi-isomorphism $p_k:T_k\to C_k$ which equals the map $q_k:B\to C_k$, $q_ke_n=j_n^{(k)}$, on the unshifted summand and zero on the shifted summand. Hence, for $v_k:B\to T_k$, $v_k(b)=(b,0)$, one has $p_kv_ke_n=j_n^{(k)}$ for every $n\geq0$.

Define $K^r:B^r\to B^{r-1}$ by $K^re_n^r=-e_{n+1}^{r-1}H^r$, using the coproduct universal property in each degree. On every summand, $(d_BK+Kd_B)e_n=-e_{n+1}(t_1-t_2)=(u_1-u_2)e_n$, so $d_BK+Kd_B=u_1-u_2$. The triangular map $F:T_1\to T_2$, $F^r(b,c)=(b+K^{r+1}c,c)$, is a chain map: its two differential composites have first coordinates $d_Bb+d_BKc+u_2c$ and $d_Bb+u_1c-Kd_Bc$, equal by that identity, and both have second coordinate $-d_Bc$. Its inverse is $(b,c)\mapsto(b-Kc,c)$. Moreover $Fv_1e_n=v_2e_n$ identically for every $n$, including $n=0$. These are direct matrix and coproduct calculations with the displayed cone differential.

source.place: Tag 014E (definition-cone), in the convention of def-weil-abstract-derived-category; explicit agent comparison and localization calculation.

proof.text: Because $p_1,p_2$ are quasi-isomorphisms and $F$ is a chain isomorphism, $\gamma=Q(p_2)\circ Q(F)\circ Q(p_1)^{-1}$ is an isomorphism $Q(C_1)\to Q(C_2)$. For each $n\geq0$, step 3 gives $Q(p_1)^{-1}Q(j_n^{(1)})=Q(v_1e_n)$, and step 4 then gives $\gamma Q(j_n^{(1)})=Q(p_2Fv_1e_n)=Q(p_2v_2e_n)=Q(j_n^{(2)})$. This proves the required normalization on every leg. All constructions use arbitrary integer degrees, so no boundedness or continuity hypothesis is needed.
